Metadata consistency checklist
Before opening a pull request:

title: Workflow
text: VirMarkDB documents how the database is generated, how marker-specific HMM profiles are built and applied, and how the database is refined through assessment-guided detection of missing or underrepresented diversity. The same overall workflow framework is used for the three viral groups currently covered (giant viruses, phages, and RNA viruses) with marker-specific search strategies. Each genome is searched only against the marker profiles relevant to its taxonomic scope.

title: Workflow
text:
Pipeline

1 · ORF prediction: ORFs are predicted from each genome with Prodigal in metagenomic mode (prodigal -p meta). Script: 02_prodigal.bash
2 · Alignment: Locally prepared marker reference proteins are aligned with MAFFT (mafft --ep 0 --genafpair --maxiterate 1000). Script: 03_align_markers.bash
3 · HMM profile construction: Local reference alignments are converted to HMM profiles with HMMER hmmbuild. The RdRp profiles are supplied by RdRp-scan instead. Script: 04_hmmbuild.bash
4 · HMM search: Predicted ORF proteomes are searched using hmmsearch for the locally built marker profiles and hmmscan for RdRp-scan. Searches use a full-sequence E-value threshold of 1e-5 and export domain-level results (--domtblout). Genome-to-marker assignments come from genome_marker_map.tsv. Script: 05_hmmsearch.bash
5 · Hit selection: For each ORF, the best HMM hit is selected based on the highest full-sequence bit score, followed by the lowest E-value. Candidate ORFs are then ranked within each genome and marker group using the same criteria. For RdRp, only the best-ranked ORF is retained, and the envelope (env_from–env_to) of the highest-scoring domain of its selected HMM hit is extracted. For the other markers, the complete ORF is retained, with additional copies included if they satisfy both the score and length ratios specified below. Finally, sequences shorter than 25% of the median extracted protein length for their marker group are excluded. Script: 06_final_results.R | Filter | Threshold | |—|—| | Score ratio relative to best hit | ≥ 0.80 | | ORF length ratio relative to best hit | ≥ 0.80 |
The two copy-retention thresholds apply to markers other than RdRp. The final length filter applies to all markers.

title: Database
text:
Why marker groups exist
Some marker genes are too divergent across viral lineages to be represented by a single HMM profile. VirMarkDB solves this with marker groups: each one ties together a marker gene, a taxonomic scope, a reference protein set, and an associated HMM resource. The Nucleocytoviricota and gp23 profiles are constructed locally, whereas RdRp detection uses the external RdRp-scan profile database. This keeps a common marker-gene framework across the database while letting each lineage be represented by a profile calibrated on its own reference sequences.






Note



This page describes the concept. The mechanics (how mapfile.tsv encodes marker groups and drives the pipeline) are covered once, in Workflow → Marker-group configuration.

title: About
text:
Notes and limitations
ORF prediction. ORFs are predicted with Prodigal in metagenomic mode. This approach is practical and robust, but some viral coding sequences may still be difficult to predict correctly. Introns, inteins, sequencing artefacts, or internal stop codons may lead to truncated or fragmented predicted proteins.
Partial genome records. Some source genomes are partial. Missing markers in those entries may reflect incomplete sequence coverage rather than true biological absence.
HMM profile performance. Profile sensitivity depends on the diversity, quality, and taxonomic coverage of the seed reference protein sets. Under-represented lineages may show lower detection rates.
Marker-group scope. Marker groups link a gene, a taxonomic scope and its associated HMM resource; RdRp uses external RdRp-scan profiles rather than a locally built HMM. Divergent lineages outside current marker-group scope may not be detected reliably.
Missing value interpretation. NA or zero values in marker presence tables mean not detected or not retained under the current workflow and thresholds, not confirmed biological absence.
External protein assessment. The external protein assessment is an empirical procedure designed to identify potentially missing or underrepresented marker diversity in VirMarkDB. It should not be interpreted as a formal performance benchmark based on a ground-truth dataset.
Current taxonomic scope. The database currently covers three viral groups: giant viruses (Nucleocytoviricota), phages (Pantevenvirales, via g23), and RNA viruses (Orthornavirae, via rdrp). Additional viral groups will be added as suitable marker references and genome mappings become available.

title: VirMarkDB
text:
A curated reference database of viral marker-gene sequences for giant viruses, phages and RNA viruses
VirMarkDB provides protein/nucleotide sequences for ten conserved marker genes across three viral groups: giant viruses (Nucleocytoviricota), phages (Pantevenvirales) and RNA viruses (Orthornavirae), built from ICTV-derived taxonomy.

title: Files & formats
text:
Markers
Organised by taxonomic group and marker: markers/<group_id>/<marker>/







File
Description




<marker_group_id>_protein.fasta
Retained marker protein sequences (the selected HMM domain envelope for RdRp; otherwise the retained ORF)


<marker_group_id>_nucleotide.fasta
Corresponding nucleotide sequences of the retained marker regions


<marker_group_id>_virus_orf_description.tsv
Per-ORF table with HMM hit metrics and virus metadata




Protein FASTA header
>orf_name marker Kingdom;Phylum;Class;Order;Family;Genus;Species


ORF annotation file
The ORF annotation file contains the final selected viral marker-gene sequences retained in VirMarkDB. Each row corresponds to one detected marker ORF associated with a viral genome.







Column
Description




orf_name
Identifier of the retained ORF sequence


virus_id
Unique identifier of the viral genome/accession


group_id
Lowercase marker scope identifier (e.g. nucleocytoviricota, orthornavirae, pantevenvirales)


marker
Marker-gene identifier


evalue
Full-sequence HMMER E-value for the selected hit


score
Full-sequence HMMER bit score for the selected hit


ORF_length_aa
Length of the original predicted ORF in amino acids


marker_length_AA
Length of the exported marker protein sequence in amino acids


marker_length_NT
Length of the exported marker nucleotide sequence in nucleotides


position_start
Predicted ORF start coordinate on the source nucleotide sequence (Prodigal)


position_end
Predicted ORF end coordinate on the source nucleotide sequence (Prodigal)


ali_from
Start position of the HMMER alignment on the original predicted ORF


ali_to
End position of the HMMER alignment on the original predicted ORF


env_from
Start of the selected HMMER domain envelope on the original predicted ORF


env_to
End of the selected HMMER domain envelope on the original predicted ORF


Species
Viral species associated with the genome


Virus_names
Virus name(s) associated with the genome









Note



For RdRp, ali_from, ali_to, env_from and env_to refer to the original ORF, while the exported FASTA contains only the selected domain envelope. The exported protein therefore begins at position 1 of that extracted region.
